chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from Ibn Abi Umayr from Abu Ayyub from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'It is not fitting for anyone to take from the soil surrounding the Kaaba, and if he takes anything of that, he must return it.'

And whoever finds something in the Sanctuary (Haram), it is not permissible for him to take it; if he takes it, he must announce it for a year. If the owner comes, [he returns it]; otherwise, he gives it in charity, and he bears the cost of its replacement if the owner comes and is not satisfied with it. And if he finds [something] outside the Sanctuary, he must announce it for a year, then it is like his own property; he does with it what he wishes, except that he is also liable [for its value].

key_terms.الْحَرَمِ: The Sanctuary (specifically the Haram in Mecca)
key_terms.يُعَرِّفْهُ: He must announce it (declare its finding)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on taking soil from around the Kaaba and handling lost property in the Haram?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) distinguishes between the sanctity of the Kaaba's soil, which must be returned if taken, and general lost property within the Haram, requiring a year of announcement and charity if unclaimed. This ruling highlights the specific legal status of the Haram's contents, where the finder acts as a trustee liable for the item's value if the owner rejects the returned object, contrasting with items found outside the Haram which become the finder's property after announcement.
